content:
Apple TV has just added a batch of classic movies for subscribers, rolled out ahead of a particularly strong fall lineup.

Apple TV has expanded its library with new films ahead of a major fall slate.

There's a lot of buzz around movies right now. Box office hits like "Blossom Apple," "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," and "Obsession" have sparked cultural moments, and the movie business is looking strong.

It looks like Apple wants in on the action too.

This week, Apple TV added a large batch of acclaimed movies for subscribers to watch for free. The exact list varies slightly by region, but in the U.S. market, viewers can find titles like "The Martian," "Arrival," "Eye in the Sky," "The Big Sick," "Memories of Murder," and "21 Jump Street."

With this addition, Apple's library size nearly doubled overnight.

Just because Apple bought the rights to these movies doesn't mean the company has given up on its original films. In fact, this influx comes ahead of a loaded fall release calendar.

Here are six new films coming to Apple TV this fall:

  • September 4: "Mayday"
  • October 2: "The Last First: Winter K2"
  • October 9: "Matchbox The Movie"
  • October 16: "Tenzing"
  • November 13: "Being Heumann"
  • November 25: "Way of the Warrior Kid"

Apple has long tried to walk a line between "Oscar bait" and "crowd-pleasers." This fall, it looks like there's roughly a 50/50 split.

"Mayday," "Matchbox," and "Way of the Warrior Kid" all appear to be breezy action-comedies starring the likes of Ryan Reynolds and John Cena. Meanwhile, "Being Heumann," "Tenzing," and "The Last First" are clearly aiming for awards season.

Apple has continued to find success on the TV side, with recent returns like "Ted Lasso." Whether the company's ambitions in film pay off in the same way remains to be seen.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, or it can be bundled with other services through Apple One for a discount.
